law_refs.quote: on or after the 9th day of June, 1952

tests.objects: Tenant actor described as respondent or respondents; alleged Wine merchant transferee; wine-shop operation said by respondents to exist since 1985 under a licence arrangement; DTTDC named by respondents as licensee. The sources do not conclusively establish whether the petitioner's unnamed Wine merchant and DTTDC are identical.
tests.opposition: The respondents dispute that the 1985 arrangement constitutes subletting, assignment or parting with possession. The precise identity correspondence between the alleged Wine merchant and the named DTTDC licensee is unverified. Nevertheless, both accounts place the disputed wine-selling arrangement after the statutory date.

tests.rationale: The petitioner expressly dates the alleged disposition after 9 June 1952, and the respondents independently describe wine-shop use beginning in 1985. The temporal condition is supported for the disputed wine-selling arrangement, without resolving its legal classification or assuming that every third-party description identifies the same entity.

law_refs.quote: In subletting there exists the relationship of landlord and tenant as between the tenant and his sub-tenant and all the incidents of letting or tenancy have to be found, namely the transfer of an interest in the estate payment of rent, and the right to possession as against the tenant in respect of the Premises sublet.

tests.objects: Potential subletting by the respondent or respondents to an unnamed Wine merchant; DTTDC separately identified in the respondent's licence account; wine-selling operation in the tenanted shop. Identity equivalence is not established.
tests.opposition: The petitioner alleges subletting. The respondents deny a subtenancy and assert that DTTDC operated under a licence, paying monthly commission rather than rent. They also assert that the shop was under the possession of the wine shop, introducing a factual issue about the extent of the operator's rights. No prior court finding in the allowed sources resolves these competing characterizations.

opposition_refs.quote: It is denied that the respondent has sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the premises under the tenancy of the respondent to a Wine Merchant
the shop in question is under the possession of wine shop by virtue of License Deed executed between DTTDC and the respondents

tests.gap_reason: The licence deed's operative terms are not supplied. The record does not establish whether the alleged Wine merchant is DTTDC, whether any payment is legally rent, whether an interest in the premises was transferred or whether the operator possessed a right against the tenant. These facts are decisive to the complete subletting test.
tests.rationale: The petitioner's subletting allegation and respondents' licence-and-commission account conflict. The description 'licence' is a party characterization, and the purported deed is mentioned rather than reproduced. Without the relationship, transfer, payment and possession-right facts tied to the same identified counterparty, the full tenancy-incidents proposition cannot be affirmed or refuted.

law_refs.quote: In assignment the tenant has to divest himself of all the rights that he has as a tenant.

tests.objects: Alleged assignment of the respondent's tenancy rights to a Wine merchant; respondents' separate identification of DTTDC as a licensee. The transferee identity and scope of assigned rights remain contested.
tests.opposition: The respondents expressly deny assignment and assert retained legal possession and an agreement described as a licence. The petitioner alleges assignment but provides no terms of an assignment instrument or description of divested rights in the supplied excerpts.

opposition_refs.quote: It is denied that the respondent has sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession

tests.gap_reason: No operative transfer document, defined rights conveyed or evidence establishing the tenant's complete divestment of tenancy rights is supplied. The named licensee's relationship to the petitioner's alleged transferee is also unverified.
tests.rationale: The petitioner invokes assignment while the respondents deny it and describe retained rights. These are opposing party positions without a supplied adjudicative finding or contractual terms sufficient to determine complete divestment. The proposition therefore remains unresolved.

tests.gap_reason: It is not established whether the wine operator obtained exclusive physical control and a legal right to possession that wholly ousted the tenant, or merely a revocable right of use. The supplied legal test requires both physical and legal dispossession. Neither the legal rights nor the counterparty correspondence can be determined from the competing pleadings alone.

tests.rationale: The petitioner directly alleges absence of written consent, while the respondents plead permission from a deceased landlord and deny the statutory allegation. The respondents' claimed permission is not established as written, but neither does the lack of an exhibited instrument prove its absence. The supplied law provides no additional consent doctrine or burden rule that resolves this factual conflict.

law_refs.quote: So long as the lessee retains the legal possession of the whole of the premises he does not commit a breach of law against parting with the possession by allowing other people to use the same.
If there is anything in the nature of a right to concurrent user there is no parting with possession
The mere user by other persons is no parting with Possession so long as the tenant retains the legal possession himself

tests.objects: Claimed retention of legal possession by respondent or respondents while DTTDC used the tenanted shop for wine sales. The link between DTTDC and the petitioner's unnamed Wine merchant remains unproved.
tests.opposition: The petitioner alleges actual parting with possession to a Wine merchant. The respondents themselves describe the shop as being under the possession of the wine shop, while simultaneously asserting that legal possession remains with them. No actual licence terms or prior court finding establish the tenant's right to concurrent use, terminate the arrangement or recover possession.

opposition_refs.quote: The respondent has sub-let, assigned or otherwise parted with the possession of the premises under the tenancy of the respondent to a Wine merchant
the shop in question is under the possession of wine shop by virtue of License Deed executed between DTTDC and the respondents

tests.gap_reason: The decisive factual and contractual issues are the tenant's actual retained right to possession, any right of concurrent use, the exclusivity of the wine operator's possession, and the enforceable termination or re-entry rights under the purported licence. The source also leaves the counterparty identity relationship unresolved.
tests.rationale: The respondents explicitly assert legal possession and describe a licence rather than a tenancy, supporting their position that the arrangement permits retained possession. But these are contested party assertions without a supplied adjudication or the operative agreement. The court-adopted qualification requires an assessment of actual retained legal rights, which cannot be established conclusively from the available material. A positive result on this negative-polarity test would defeat only the parting-with-possession route.

tests.rationale: Both sides link the disputed wine-selling arrangement to the shop under the respondent's tenancy. The legal efficacy of the disposition and the identity of the recipient remain separate, unresolved issues.
